definitions.explanation: the ability to remember or the state of remembering something; a sense of having experienced something before
a written record made as a reminder or for reference

examples.japanese: そんなことを{言|い}った{覚|おぼ}えはない。
examples.english: I don't remember saying such a thing.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}に{会|あ}った{覚|おぼ}えがある。
examples.english: I have a recollection of having met him.

examples.japanese: {身|み}に{覚|おぼ}えのないことで{疑|うたが}われて{困|こま}った。
examples.english: I was troubled by being suspected of something I had no memory of doing.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{内容|ないよう}を{覚|おぼ}え{書|が}きにまとめた。
examples.english: I compiled the contents of the meeting into a memorandum.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}なことは{覚|おぼ}え{書|が}きにして{残|のこ}しておこう。
examples.english: Let's put important things down in notes so they're preserved.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {覚|おぼ}える (to remember). In sense 1, it refers to the subjective feeling or awareness of remembering something. In sense 2, it refers to a written note or memorandum.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {覚|おぼ}えがある: to have a memory of, to recall
- {覚|おぼ}えがない: to have no memory of, to not recall
- {身|み}に{覚|おぼ}えがない: to have no recollection of doing something (strong denial)
- {覚|おぼ}え{書|が}き: memorandum, written notes

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {覚|おぼ}えが{早|はや}い: quick to learn
- {覚|おぼ}えが{悪|わる}い: slow to learn, having poor memory
- {覚|おぼ}えがめでたい: to be in someone's good graces, to be well-regarded

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {記憶|きおく}: memory — more formal, refers to the faculty or stored content of memory
- {思|おも}い{出|で}: memories, reminiscence — emphasizes nostalgic or emotional recollection
